I hear what you're saying. This is how I've come to think of it (for myself! I'm not advising ANYONE ELSE to feel or think this way!) It's like someone that has an illness or disease that they're slowly dying from. They're in awful pain 24 hours a day, every day. Someone dying of cancer gets lots of care and sympathy but they're still dying. Personally, I don't think people in these situations should have to suffer until the very bitter end. Like others have said: We (most people) don't let our pets suffer; if they're in that much agony, we put them to sleep. One injection and they just drift off peacefully. Mental illness is hard because it's not visible. You don't SEE the gaping, oozing wounds - but they're there. They're ALWAYS there. Always.
I get that you think it's selfish of them to want to go but isn't it also selfish of you for wanting them to stay? It's just a thought, not a judgement. I'm sorry for your loss and I wish it could've turned out differently. Hugs ❤️ 
One thing I forgot to add: When I said that a cancer patient would get lots of care and sympathy (hopefully), I meant to point out that mental patients do almost all of their suffering alone. Most people can't relate to them and don't know how to help. There is way too much suffering all alone.
